rules: English public copy only unless the owner asks otherwise.
No Steam, demo, release, wishlist, performance, or gameplay-screenshot claim without proof.
If the post feels like a brand manager wrote it, do not publish it.

items.text:
Opened the accounts before the good shots are ready.
For now I am mostly deleting frames that look cool and say nothing.
items.why: Second public note after the intro. It admits the account is early and makes the screenshot standard concrete.

items.text:
Profile art for Teni Games.
Not gameplay. Just the account getting dressed before the real shots are worth posting.

instagram.reason: Instagram web posting is foreground-heavy and easy to botch; use only after a verified post flow or mobile pass.

items.why: Good caption, but the platform path is not reliable enough for unattended posting yet.

items.text:
Current rule for Submerge screenshots:
if the frame does not tell you what the player should worry about, it is not ready.

x.reason: Stronger with the first real screenshot or rejected-shot comparison.

bluesky.reason: Stronger with the first real screenshot or rejected-shot comparison.

items.why: Useful positioning, but it should land with proof instead of becoming abstract filler.

items.text:
The ocean is not the hook.
The machine failing under it is.

x.reason: Good short line, but too slogan-like as a third same-day post before screenshots.

bluesky.reason: Good short line, but too slogan-like as a third same-day post before screenshots.

items.why: Keep for later, after a clip or machinery shot can carry it.

items.text:
The first useful Submerge screenshot is probably not the big ocean shot.

It is a pump, a hatch, a gauge, and a way back that already looks worse than the way in.

x.reason: Needs a pressure-room/current-build image. Text alone would sound like positioning instead of proof.

bluesky.reason: Needs a pressure-room/current-build image. Text alone would sound like positioning instead of proof.

telegram.reason: Can become a dev-feed post only with a rough frame or rejected-shot comparison.

items.why: Current best next public beat: first proof should sell machinery/pressure/return-route readability, not ocean mood.

items.text:
A pretty ocean shot is easy to make.

A useful one tells you what will fail first.

x.reason: Use with a rejected beauty frame or side-by-side proof, not as a third text-only post.

bluesky.reason: Use with a rejected beauty frame or side-by-side proof, not as a third text-only post.

items.why: Keeps the public standard human and concrete while avoiding empty daily posting.

items.text:
The salvage tool should not feel like a loot vacuum.

It should feel like a witness.

x.reason: Requires a tool/salvage image or clip where the object, scar, route, and risk are visible.

bluesky.reason: Requires a tool/salvage image or clip where the object, scar, route, and risk are visible.

reddit.reason: Could become a critique question after subreddit rule checks and a real salvage frame.

items.why: Future differentiator: salvage as evidence/risk, not resource sparkle.
